behavior_change_from_previous: a minor release on 0.39.0: --sudo TEXT runs a command as root on a platform's exec channel (sudo -S -p with karvi's prompt, no sh -c; the password the answering backend's enable field, NETSUDO, or NETENABLE under netvars, else sudo -n), a target on a shell refused channel_shell_sudo_refused, the record's and the audit's privilege sudo; --sleep DURATION waits before the next command, the rerun files writing each sleep back; a commands-file line or a platform's crun-commands entry beginning --sudo or --sleep is that statement, a malformed one refused commands_file_sudo_invalid or commands_file_sleep_invalid; a lone --cmd or --sudo takes the words after it, and after -- every word; a device of - reads standard input as --tf - does; --debug names the SSH algorithms the native transport negotiated; the command record has no command_sha256; each schema counter is written once, in the package that owns its schema, the schema files' titles and $ids naming none, and verify-shipped.sh compares the shipped executable's counters with this manifest; verify-release.sh reads karvi's output whole before checking it; execution plan 17, command record 5, and audit 3 move, every other counter is 0.39.0's (configuration schema 6, registry 33, daemon IPC 12, job manifest and summary 5, plan report 4, credential package 2, scoreboard 5); Go and every module are 0.39.0's; the first submission after the upgrade drains a 0.39.0 daemon; see CHANGELOG.md

build.dependencies: vendored (go.mod, go.sum, vendor/); built with no network

daemon_upgrade_recovery.job_submission_schema: exact-current-only (the client's IPC schema and build)
daemon_upgrade_recovery.automatic_replacement: a client launching its own daemon (daemon.launch client) drains a daemon of another build at its own schema: idle, it exits and the client starts its own in the same invocation; busy, it finishes its jobs and exits after the last, each submission meanwhile refused daemon_draining (exit 112); a service account's daemon (daemon.launch systemd) is never drained by a client, and its unit is restarted
daemon_upgrade_recovery.incompatible_run_error: daemon_incompatible (a daemon of a newer IPC schema); daemon_draining (a drained daemon finishing its jobs)
daemon_upgrade_recovery.actual_lifecycle_replay: not run: the newest release whose daemon IPC schema (11) differs from this client's (12) is v0.29.0, whose daemon predates the drain that exits and listens on daemon.sock, which this client never reaches; the compatibility example ran before the number was committed: beside the released v0.39.0 daemon, at this client's schema and of another build, the client's daemon status stacked the two builds (compatible: false), its run's exercise drained the idle daemon and started its own (exit 0, no device contacted), and with the older daemon holding a job on the fake device the client's run was refused daemon_draining (exit 112), the daemon exiting after the job (evidence/ipc-schema-compat.log)
